name: Uganda
summary: Six horizontal stripes of black, yellow and red, repeated, with a white disc in the centre bearing a grey crowned crane. Adopted at independence in 1962.
origin: The colours come from the flag of the ruling Uganda People's Congress at independence. The Minister of Justice, Grace Ibingira, is credited with the design, adopted on 9 October 1962.
The crowned crane had been the badge of the British Uganda Protectorate and was kept as the national bird.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: African brotherhood, the blood that connects all Africans.

symbols.name: Grey crowned crane
symbols.description: A crane standing on one leg in a white disc, facing the hoist.
symbols.meaning: The national bird; the raised leg symbolises the country moving forward.

history.label: Uganda Protectorate
history.note: Blue ensign with a crane badge.

facts: The crane is said to be raising its leg to show the country moving forward.
The crane is also on the coat of arms, together with a Uganda kob.
clues: Black, yellow and red stripes repeated twice, with a crane in a white disc.
Its bird stands on one leg to show forward movement.
Its crane was the badge of a British protectorate.
